answer.question: How does a pond affect a small Nocatee turf layout?
answer.answer: Where Florida’s residential standard applies, turf generally needs a 10-foot separation from the pond’s high-water line, with an exception for a separating seawall or bulkhead. Swales and pond littoral areas stay clear. Establish that boundary and any maintenance access before deciding how much yard can be turfed.

blocks.kicker: Between the lanai and the boundary
blocks.h2: Choose the most useful area first.
paras: A pet area close to the door, a lawn for everyday use and a compact green each need different space. On a narrow lot, compare one primary use before trying to fit all three. For putting, leave standing room and a clear route around the surface.
Many newer yards have limited shade. Think about when the area will be used and how people or pets can get out of full sun; turf can become hot.

blocks.h2: Confirm who controls each part of the plan.
paras: Nocatee has different neighborhood associations and CDDs, and spans St. Johns and Duval counties. Use the exact property and community when requesting the applicable requirements. An architectural committee’s response and CDD conditions should be checked for the actual work area.

Mark pond edges, swales, easements and preserve boundaries on the plan. A rear fence does not establish permission to use every strip within it. Bring the written conditions to the estimate, together with existing irrigation and drainage information.
